clue.text: Quote work both contrary and lyrical

indicators.note: both pieces turned the wrong way round together, so the two words are read backwards as one run

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone cites a piece of writing that is both argumentative and songlike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both contrary' turns CITEOP round as one run, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe expressive, song-like language suited to verse, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Musical compositions are humourless in retrospect

definitions.note: plural: the answer is the Latin plural of opus

indicators.note: looking back, so the run of letters is read from the end towards the start

parts.note: PO, as in po-faced, means humourless and disapproving

explanation.surface: A remark that certain pieces of music seem dour when looked back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns AREPO round as one run. The answer here is not the stage work but the plural of opus.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus means a numbered musical work, and its Latin plural is the word needed, so several works fit.

clue.text: Ineffective and also extremely tough? Not as much

parts.note: too means also, as in 'me too'

indicators.note: the extreme ends of the word tough are its first and last letters

parts.note: less means a smaller amount, not as much

explanation.surface: Asks whether something is both feeble and very hard, then denies it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking teeth is the idiom for a rule or body without power to enforce, hence weak and futile.

clue.text: Birthplace of rock?

parts.note: a baby's bed is the place where life is nurtured, and it is a bed that one rocks; the question mark flags that this is not rock music

explanation.definitionFit: A baby's swinging bed is also the figurative birthplace or origin of anything, and parents rock it.

clue.text: Sweet Delia ultimately did wrong stuffing prune

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the name Delia, its last letter
the shuffled letters are packed inside the word for prune, like filling

parts.note: to prune a plant is to crop it

indicators.note: done wrong, the three letters of did are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity cook makes a mistake filling a dried plum with something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is a famous British TV cookery writer; 'prune' is the verb, not the dried plum.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled sour-sharp lozenge is a classic British confectionery, a hard sweet.

clue.text: Farming can be brutal — with onset of rain disrupting better half year

parts.note: animal, as an adjective, means bestial or brutal

indicators.note: breaking into, so the letter goes inside the run of letters beside it

parts.note: a jocular term for one's spouse, here the man of the couple

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so take the first letter of rain

explanation.surface: Agriculture can be cruel, especially when a wet spell upsets a spouse's year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupting' puts R (from 'onset of rain') between HUSBAND and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock rearing is a branch of agriculture, so the phrase names a kind of farming work.

clue.text: Fashionable drinks by the sound of it — these could have an edge

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

indicators.note: says the drinks word is heard rather than spelt, matching a word that sounds the same

parts.note: ciders are apple drinks

explanation.surface: Trendy beverages, apparently, give their drinkers some advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: CIDERS and SIDERS sound alike; the spelt letters complete the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: People with privileged inside knowledge have an advantage, an edge, over everyone else.

clue.text: Fanny Cradock's heart almost flipped for Austen hero

indicators.note: turned over, so the run is read from right to left
nearly the central part of the name, a run taken from inside the words Fanny Cradock

explanation.surface: A TV cook's emotions nearly turn over at the sight of a romantic hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart almost' takes YCRAD from inside Fanny Cradock, and 'flipped' reverses it. Fanny Cradock was a famous British TV cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Fitzwilliam is the proud male lead of Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen.

clue.text: Band of men with revolutionary talents on the rise

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: arts are skills or talents

explanation.surface: A group of rebels whose skills are growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' turns ARTS into STRA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of musicians playing together is a band in the musical sense.

clue.text: Stack endless bricks

indicators.note: without ends, so the first and last letters of bricks are dropped

explanation.surface: An instruction to pile up an unending supply of building blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A haystack is called this, so it is a stack of hay or straw.

clue.text: V&A library originally next to foyer — a blissful spot

parts.note: the Victoria and Albert Museum, shortened to its letters

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an entrance hall is a foyer

explanation.surface: The museum's library, set beside its entrance lobby, is a delightful place.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is a great London museum, the Victoria and Albert.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth, the hall of slain heroes is a paradise, a heavenly place of bliss.

clue.text: Spooner's brown horse passed resting place

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds of the two words are exchanged

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
passed away, so dead

explanation.surface: A dead reddish-brown horse, as the Reverend Spooner might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BAY DEAD gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch you can lie on in the daytime is a bed for resting on.

clue.text: Sidekick runs away from attacker

indicators.note: taken away from, so the named letters are removed

parts.note: a raider is one who attacks
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs; runs being plural, both R's go

explanation.surface: An assistant flees from an assailant.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant or right-hand helper is a sidekick, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Longing to travel given ticklish verbal undertaking

parts.note: itchy and ticklish both describe an irritating skin sensation

indicators.note: spoken, so the word for undertaking is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a feat is a notable task undertaken

explanation.surface: Wanderlust prompted by an irritating spoken promise.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a restless desire to go off and wander or explore.

clue.text: Present song lacks core evidence of pedigree

parts.note: here means present, as in a roll call

indicators.note: the central letter of the song word is missing

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: A current song without its heart proves nothing of one's lineage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks core' removes the middle T of DITTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Traits passed from parents to offspring show inherited lineage, so inheritance shows one's breeding.

clue.text: Treat fellow with contempt and pull leg?

parts.note: to dis someone is to treat them with contempt
a fellow of a society is a member

explanation.surface: Sneer at a colleague and tease him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treat ... with contempt' supplies DIS, read after the member it is aimed at. 'Pull leg' is not teasing but literally tearing a limb off.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut or tear off limbs; pulling off a leg is a literal instance.

clue.text: Expression of surprise in the wake of 'Rolling Stone Ron's outdoor type!'

indicators.note: following behind, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: Ron Wood is the guitarist of the Rolling Stones; the possessive adds the final S
'Man!' is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Exclaiming at a rock guitarist being a lover of fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: A forester or person who lives and works in forests is a typical outdoorsman.

clue.text: Charlie is so right to wear smalls providing grip for legs

indicators.note: the smalls are worn around the other letters, so they enclose them

parts.note: two smalls, each S, the abbreviation for small
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie's underwear is so tight it grips his legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smalls' is British slang for underwear; here it is two S's for small, wrapping CISSOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling hold in which the legs lock around an opponent is named after cutting shears.

clue.text: Timothy and Rafe shedding pounds in health resorts

indicators.note: losing, so the named letters are taken out

parts.note: Timothy Spall and his son Rafe are both English actors
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, here doubled for pounds

explanation.surface: Two actors lose weight at a wellness retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Places with mineral springs or wellness treatments are health resorts.

clue.text: It's soft in the head to play the xylophone

definitions.text: It's soft in the head to play the xylophone

parts.words: It's soft in the head to play the xylophone
parts.note: a xylophone beater has a soft padded head; 'soft in the head' pretends to mean foolish

explanation.definitionFit: A hammer-like beater with a padded head is used to strike the bars of a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Shy bridesmaid content to be cross

indicators.note: contents are what something holds inside, so the run sits within the words

explanation.surface: A timid wedding attendant is happy to be angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'happy' but means contents. 'cross' is not anger here.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross between two breeds or species is a mixed offspring.

clue.text: Right how-d'ye-do now and then where cowboys compete

indicators.note: occasionally, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A proper greeting, occasionally, at a cowboy contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of HOWDYEDO give ODEO.
explanation.definitionFit: A show of riding and roping skills is an event where ranch hands compete.

clue.text: A rat and mice dissected — it's educational

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel, a rat

indicators.note: cut up, so the letters of mice are rearranged

explanation.surface: A laboratory scene: dissecting rodents is instructive.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to scholarship and teaching, so to do with education.

clue.text: Have enough of critic on silent pictures

indicators.note: take just enough of the words to spell the answer, a run found inside them

explanation.surface: Fed up with a reviewer of silent films.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious images or symbolic representations are pictures.

clue.text: Fine due over brawl

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: turned over, so due reads backwards

explanation.surface: A penalty is payable after a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running bitter quarrel is a kind of fight or brawl.

clue.text: Cliff pursuing hit ideally neither intellectual nor downmarket

indicators.note: following, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: a batsman ideally hits the ball in the middle of the bat; to middle it is to strike it cleanly
the brow of a hill or cliff is its top edge

explanation.surface: Cliff Richard's hit is pleasantly mid-range in taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste that is between high culture and low appeal is moderate, average in sophistication.

clue.text: A time to regret originally pining over lawyer

indicators.note: taking the origin, the first letter, of regret
turned over, so this word reads backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing, a pining

explanation.surface: Someone yearning with remorse for a while before going to a solicitor.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US, a qualified legal practitioner is called this, a lawyer.

clue.text: Harvesters may do this right into the small hours

indicators.note: placed into, so this letter goes inside the others

explanation.surface: Farm workers toil right through to the early morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Separating grain from husks is a harvest task done by farmhands.
